action: Autopay card payers in Poland: check your transaction history and report any transaction you do not recognise to your card-issuing bank; treat messages or calls that cite this incident with caution.
date_note: Date Autopay says it detected the unauthorized access; reported 14-15 November
exec: A Polish payment operator reports unauthorized access to part of its payment data; scope is not stated, so merchants and cardholders cannot yet judge exposure.
plain: Polish online payment company Autopay says someone got into part of its systems and some payment data it handles. It says payments kept working and has not said how many people are affected.
summary: Autopay S.A. says it detected unauthorized access on 11 November to part of its infrastructure and to part of the payment data it processes, and cannot entirely rule out that data was copied. The company says transaction processing was not affected. A spokesperson described a new type of attack with heavy use of AI tools; no number of affected people has been stated.
title: Autopay (Poland) reports unauthorized access to payment data, says attack used AI tools

validation.note: money.pl and Spider's Web both relay Autopay's own statement; no independent confirmation of scope. The Japanese headline's claim that banks blocked cards is not in either page read.

review.note: Compared title, 11 Nov detection, no affected number, copying not ruled out, AI statement against money.pl (PAP) and Spider's Web; narrowed 'payments and services not affected' to transaction processing; softened 'ignore' to 'treat with caution'.
